"ETERNAL WORLD — OPEN-WORLD SURVIVAL RPG

Create an open-world survival RPG game, with realistic 3D graphics, for Android and iOS devices.

The game should offer free exploration, combat, character progression, building, resource gathering, creatures (mobs), weapons, swords, special powers, and online multiplayer.

The goal is to create a survival and adventure experience in a gigantic world, where each player can create their own story.

1. MAIN MENU

When opening the game, present a cinematic start screen with:
- Game name: ETERNAL WORLD.
- NEW GAME button.
- CONTINUE button.
- MULTIPLAYER button.
- SETTINGS button.
- CUSTOMIZE CHARACTER button.

Create an animated 3D background scene, showing the game world.

2. CHARACTER CREATION

Before starting the adventure, the player must customize their character.

Add:
- Choice between male and female characters.
- Different faces.
- Hair and hairstyles.
- Hair colors.
- Skin tones.
- Eyes.
- Starting clothes.
- Pants and boots.
- Accessories.
- Armor.

Allow viewing the character in 3D and rotating it before confirming.

The created character must appear throughout the entire game.

3. OPEN WORLD

Create a huge and explorable map, divided into different biomes:

- Dense forests.
- Snowy mountains.
- Deserts.
- Beaches and oceans.
- Caves.
- Swamps.
- Plains.
- Abandoned villages.
- Castles and ruins.
- Underground dungeons.

Each region must have its own resources, creatures, buildings, and challenges.

Add day and night cycle, dynamic weather, rain, storms, fog, and lighting changes.

4. SURVIVAL

Create survival systems with:
- Health bar.
- Hunger bar.
- Thirst bar.
- Energy.
- Body temperature.

The player must search for food, water, and materials to survive.

Allow:
- Cutting trees.
- Mining stones.
- Collecting plants.
- Hunting fictional animals.
- Fishing.
- Cooking food.
- Creating tools.
- Building shelters.

5. WEAPONS AND COMBAT

Add different categories of equipment:

*Swords*
- Wooden sword.
- Iron sword.
- Steel sword.
- Fire sword.
- Ice sword.
- Legendary sword.

*Other weapons*
- Bows.
- Axes.
- Magic staffs.
- Daggers.
- Hammers.

Each piece of equipment must have its own attributes, animations, and visual effects.

Create a combat system with:
- Normal attack.
- Special attack.
- Defense.
- Dodge.
- Combos.
- Skill bar.

6. SPECIAL POWERS

Add a power system that allows the player to unlock abilities:

- Fire.
- Ice.
- Lightning.
- Earth.
- Wind.
- Shadow.
- Light.

Each element must have different abilities.

Allow evolving powers and unlocking new abilities as the player gains experience.

7. MOBS AND CREATURES

Create creatures spread across the world:

- Goblins.
- Skeletons.
- Wolves.
- Giant spiders.
- Trolls.
- Golems.
- Dragons.
- Magical creatures.
- Dungeon bosses.

Each creature must have:
- Its own appearance.
- Animations.
- Its own behavior.
- Difficulty level.
- Amount of experience granted.

Bosses must have special abilities and exclusive rewards.

8. ONLINE MULTIPLAYER

The game must have functional online multiplayer.

Add:
- Online servers.
- Room creation.
- Friend invites.
- Player groups.
- Joint exploration.
- Cooperative combat.
- Bosses that require cooperation.
- Item trading system.
- Shared buildings.
- Player identification by name.

Allow multiple players to be in the same world and interact in real time.

Create privacy controls, player reporting and blocking, plus communication filters.

9. PROGRESSION SYSTEM

Add a level and experience system.

The player must gain XP by:
- Defeating creatures.
- Exploring regions.
- Completing quests.
- Discovering places.
- Defeating bosses.
- Crafting equipment.

At each level, allow improving attributes:
- Strength.
- Endurance.
- Speed.
- Energy.
- Magic.
- Defense.

10. INVENTORY AND CRAFTING

Create a visual inventory with slots for:
- Weapons.
- Armor.
- Food.
- Potions.
- Materials.
- Rare resources.
- Special items.

Add a crafting system, allowing combining materials to create better

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable ETERNAL WORLD survival RPG in the existing project, or a cohesive playable prototype if the full scope is not feasible.

## Requirements
- Include a cinematic menu, character customization, explorable biomes, survival, gathering, combat, progression, inventory, and crafting.
- Provide online multiplayer if possible; be clear if backend services are unavailable.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them on completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use a browser-playable prototype because the repository had no established game framework or app entrypoint.
- Represent multiplayer as a clearly labeled local preview; no server is connected.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a self-contained HTML prototype with a canvas world, menu, character setup, movement, gathering, combat, survival meters, crafting, inventory, progression, and local multiplayer preview.
- Extracted the inline JavaScript and passed `node --check` on it.

### Active
- Reconcile the prototype with the additional `game.js` and `styles.css` files present in the repository; confirm which implementation is intended to be the entrypoint.
- Verify the game in a browser and fix any runtime or UI issues.

### Blocked
- Real online multiplayer requires a backend; none is connected in the prototype.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `index.html`, `game.js`, and `styles.css` together; determine whether the latter files are a separate implementation and integrate one coherent game entrypoint.
2. Run the app using the available workflow and test menu, character setup, movement, gathering, combat, inventory, and crafting.
3. Save and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot; report assumptions and multiplayer limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Current standalone prototype and inline game logic.
- `game.js`: Additional game implementation present but not loaded by the current HTML.
- `styles.css`: Additional stylesheet present but not loaded by the current HTML.

## Important Context
- The repository initially had no app source or build configuration.
- Changes are uncommitted; repository status showed `index.html`, `game.js`, and `styles.css` as untracked.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable ETERNAL WORLD survival RPG in the existing project, or a cohesive playable prototype if the full scope is not feasible.

## Requirements
- Include a cinematic menu, character customization, explorable biomes, survival, gathering, combat, progression, inventory, and crafting.
- Provide online multiplayer if possible; be clear if backend services are unavailable.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them on completion.
- For visual checks, save a JPEG no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use a browser-playable prototype because the repository had no established game framework or app entrypoint.
- Represent multiplayer as a clearly labeled local preview; no server is connected.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a standalone `index.html` prototype with a canvas world, menu, character setup, movement, gathering, combat, survival meters, crafting, inventory, progression, and local multiplayer preview.
- Ran `node --check game.js` successfully.
- Started a local HTTP server and captured/inspected a menu screenshot at `/tmp/opencode/eternal-menu.png` (PNG; visual-check JPEG requirement remains unmet).

### Active
- Reconcile `index.html` with the separate `game.js` and `styles.css` implementation; confirm the intended entrypoint and resolve the conflicting implementations.
- Verify runtime behavior and test the main gameplay interactions in a browser.

### Blocked
- Real online multiplayer requires a backend; none is connected in the prototype.

## Next Move
1. Compare `index.html`, `game.js`, and `styles.css` and choose/integrate one coherent implementation.
2. Run the selected game in a browser; check menu, customization, movement, gathering, combat, inventory, and crafting, fixing runtime/UI issues.
3. Save and inspect the latest screenshot as a JPEG no wider than 1280px; then report assumptions and multiplayer limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Current standalone prototype with inline styling and JavaScript; does not load `game.js` or `styles.css`.
- `game.js`: Separate game implementation, not currently loaded by the HTML.
- `styles.css`: Stylesheet for the separate implementation, not currently loaded by the HTML.
- `/tmp/opencode/eternal-menu.png`: Existing inspected menu screenshot; PNG rather than required JPEG.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `game.js`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, `startup.sh`, and `styles.css` as untracked.
